text:
Predicates:
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in x.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: The security deposit for x is y.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at x is y.
Owns(x, y) ::: x owns y.
Rents(x, y) ::: x rents an apartment in y.
Allowed(x, y, z) ::: x is allowed to move into y with z.
MoreThan(x, y) ::: x is more than y.
Equal(x, y) ::: x is equal to y.

Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pets, x, pets)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x ∀y (SecurityDeposit(x, y) → (Equal(y, MonthlyRent(x, z)) ∨ MoreThan(y, MonthlyRent(x, z)))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
∀x (Rents(tom, x) ↔ (Allowed(tom, x, fluffy) ∧ ∀y (SecurityDeposit(x, y) → ¬MoreThan(y, 1500)))) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
MoreThan(2000, 1500) ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.

Conclusion:
SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, 2000) ∨ MoreThan(SecurityDeposit(oliveGarden, z), 2000) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
